Since the order in which the swords are used does not matter, the number of ways the swords can be used is a combination of the available swords.

The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

When at level $k,$ there are $k+2$ swords, so $n=k+2.$ We want to select $3$ of those, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different selections of three swords is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{k+2}{C}_{3} & =\frac{(k+2)!}{((k+2)-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{1}{3!}\cdot (\frac{(k+2)!}{(k-1)!}).\end{aligned}
$$

In part 5, we found that $\frac{(k+2)!}{(k-1)!}={k}^{3}+3{k}^{2}+2k.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{k+2}{C}_{3} & =\frac{1}{3!}\cdot (\frac{(k+2)!}{(k-1)!}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1}({k}^{3}+3{k}^{2}+2k) \\  & =\frac{{k}^{3}+3{k}^{2}+2k}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
